items.name: BA’s Best Green Bean Casserole With Step-by-Step Video
steps: Place rack in middle of oven; preheat oven to 375°. Working in batches, cook 2 lb. fresh green beans in a large pot of boiling salted water until bright green and halfway to tenderness, about 3 minutes per batch. Drain and let cool; trim stem ends.

Heat 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook ½ lb. crimini mushrooms, sliced, without stirring, until golden brown underneath, about 2 minutes. Toss and continue to cook, tossing occasionally, until browned on both sides, about 3 minutes more. Add 2 Tbsp.

unsalted butter and 2 large thyme sprigs to pan. Cook, tossing occasionally, until butter browns and mushrooms are dark brown and very tender, about 4 minutes longer. Season with kosher salt and transfer to a plate. Repeat with 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter, salt, and remaining 1 Tbsp.
extra-virgin olive oil, ½ lb. crimini mushrooms, sliced, and 2 large thyme sprigs.

Melt remaining 2 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large saucepan over medium-low. Whisk in 2 Tbsp. all-purpose flour and cook, whisking occasionally, until roux is golden brown and smells mildly nutty, about 4 minutes. Whisk in 1¼ cups whole milk and 1 cup heavy cream.

Increase heat and bring to a simmer, whisking often, and cook until béchamel sauce is thick and bubbling, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and whisk in 4 garlic cloves, finely grated, and ½ cup grated Parmesan; season with salt and freshly ground pepper.

Arrange green beans and mushrooms in a 2-qt. baking dish. Pour sauce over bean mixture (it may not look like enough, but it will get saucier as it bakes). Cover tightly with foil and bake until sauce is bubbling, 25–30 minutes.

Uncover and continue to bake until casserole is lightly browned on top and around the edges, 15–20 minutes longer. Top with ¾ cup French’s fried onions and continue to bake just until onions are slightly darker and fragrant, about 3 minutes. Let sit 10 minutes to set before serving.

Editor’s note: This green bean casserole recipe first appeared in November 2016 as part of BA’s Best, our vault of the Test Kitchen’s definitive takes on iconic dishes. Head this way for more of our go-to Thanksgiving recipes →

items.name: Braised Cabbage
ingredients: 2 pound green cabbage (1 small head or ½ large)
¾ cup dry low-calorie white wine (such as Illuminate Sauvignon Blanc or Matua Lighter Sauvignon Blanc, divided)
¾ cup vegetable (chicken or mushroom broth)
3 tablespoons concentrated tomato paste (usually found in a tube)
2 tablespoons unsalted butter (or DF butter, divided)
2 medium shallots (about 4 ounces, sliced into thin rounds (about 1 cup))
½ teaspoon black pepper (freshly ground, divided)
steps: Cut the cabbage through the core into 4 wedges, if using a small head. If using a large head, cut the cabbage through the core in half, then cut the half into 4 wedges and save the other half for another recipe.

Arrange a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 375°F. In a large liquid measuring cup or medium bowl, whisk together the white wine, broth, and tomato paste until smooth then set the sauce aside.

Warm a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in the hot skillet then add the shallots and ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring constantly, until tender, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme and cook, stirring constantly, until tender, 1 to 1 ½ minutes. Scrape into the bowl with the white wine mixture.

Melt the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter in the skillet. Arrange the cabbage wedges cut-side-down in the melted butter in a single layer and cook until the cabbage is deeply browned on the first side, 3 to 4 minutes.

Use tongs to turn the cabbage pieces over to their second cut sides and cook until the cabbage is deeply browned on the second side, 3 to 4 minutes. Turn the cabbage pieces over so that the cut slides are facing up and season the cabbage with the remaining 1 ¼ teaspoons of salt and the black pepper.

Turn the cabbage wedges over onto their cut sides again, pour the sauce into the skillet, and bring to a simmer. Spoon some of the simmering sauce over each cabbage wedge then transfer the skillet to the oven.

Roast until the cabbage is caramelized and very tender (you should be able to pierce through a cabbage wedge with a paring knife with ease) and the sauce has reduced by roughly half and thickened slightly, 35 to 45 minutes, rotating the skillet front to back once after 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with the chopped parsley and serve.

items.name: BA's Best Orecchiette With Sausage and Broccoli Rabe
ingredients: 1 lb. orecchiette (little ear-shaped pasta) or other short pasta
1 lb. hot Italian sausage, casings removed if needed
1 head of garlic, cloves separated, peeled, thinly sliced
4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter, cut into pieces
Crushed red pepper flakes (for seasoning; optional)
1 oz. Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup), plus more for serving
steps: Cut 2 large bunches broccoli rabe, trimmed, in half crosswise to separate thick stalks from thinner stems and florets. Cook thicker stalks in a medium pot of boiling salted water until crisp-tender, about 5 minutes.
Add thinner stems and florets and cook until all of the broccoli rabe is tender (the tip of a paring knife should slide through the stalks with little to no resistance), about 3 minutes.
Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet with tongs; let sit until cool enough to handle (no need to squeeze out excess water unless dripping wet). Coarsely chop into bite-size pieces.

Meanwhile, cook 1 lb. orecchiette (little ear-shaped pasta) or other short pasta in a second medium pot of boiling salted water until al dente (or use same pot with fresh salted water). Drain, reserving 2 cups pasta cooking liquid.

Heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a medium Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium-high. Cook 1 lb. hot Italian sausage, casings removed if needed, breaking up with a wooden spoon, until golden brown and nearly cooked through, about 5 minutes.

Add 1 head of garlic, cloves separated, peeled, thinly sliced, and remaining 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Cook, breaking up sausage even finer if needed and stirring often, until garlic is golden brown and softened, 3–4 minutes.
Add broccoli rabe and cook, stirring occasionally, until very tender and wilted, about 5 minutes.

Add 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter, cut into pieces, pasta, and 1 cup pasta cooking liquid. Cook, stirring often and adding more pasta cooking liquid as needed, until pasta is coated in a clingy sauce. Taste and add some crushed red pepper flakes if desired. Add 1 oz.
Parmesan, finely grated (about ½ cup), and stir, adding more pasta cooking liquid a splash at a time as needed to keep sauce smooth and shiny, until incorporated; season with salt.
Divide pasta among shallow bowls and top with more Parmesan.

items.name: Cheeseburger Soup
ingredients: 1 lb. ground beef I use 73/27 fat beef, $5.74*
1 lb. red potatoes peeled & medium dice, $1.25**
steps: Gather and prepare all ingredients.

In a large pot over medium heat, add the bacon. Cook the bacon for 10 minutes, or until it’s crispy. Using a slotted spoon, remove the bacon from the pan, leaving the grease in the pan. Set the bacon aside.

Add the ground beef, ½ tsp salt, and ½ tsp pepper. Brown the meat for 5 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks. Remove the beef from the pot, leaving as much grease in the pot, and set it aside. (see notes)
Add the onions, celery, carrot, potatoes, remaining salt, pepper, garlic powder, and dried oregano. Continue cooking for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Sprinkle in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chicken broth and milk. Bring to a simmer. Once the soup is at a simmer, continue cooking for 15 minutes, until the soup has thickened and the potatoes are tender.
Add the cheese and beef back in, and stir for 2 minutes until melted.
Garnish with sliced green onions and cooked bacon.

items.name: I really like this cookbook: Made Simple by Danielle Alvarez
Dry-Brined Turkey With Tangy Honey Glaze
ingredients: ½ cup Diamond Crystal or ¼ cup plus 1½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
1 12–14-lb. turkey, neck reserved for gravy, giblets discarded, patted dry
12 Tbsp. (1½ sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature, divided
¼ cup sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar
steps: Place ½ cup Diamond Crystal or ¼ cup plus 1½ tsp. Morton kosher salt and 1 Tbsp. light brown sugar in a small bowl and work together with your fingers until incorporated. Place one 12–14-lb.

turkey, neck reserved for gravy, giblets discarded, on a wire rack set inside a rimmed baking sheet and pat dry with paper towels. (If you don’t have this setup, place your turkey on a V-shape rack set inside a large roasting pan.

) Sprinkle salt mixture all over outside of the turkey as well as inside the cavity of the turkey, patting to adhere and nudging some into every crevice. You won’t need all of the dry brine, but it’s good to have extra since some of it will end up on the baking sheet as you season the turkey.
Chill bird, uncovered, at least 12 hours and up to 2 days.

Remove turkey from wire rack and rinse baking sheet and rack if needed (turkey will most likely release some liquid onto pan). Line baking sheet with 3 layers of foil and set rack back inside. Place turkey, breast side up, on rack and tuck wings underneath. Let turkey sit at room temperature 2–3 hours.

Place an oven rack in middle of oven; preheat oven to 450°. Using your fingers, loosen turkey skin on breast. Work 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, room temperature, under skin, spreading evenly over both breasts. Smear outside of turkey with another 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, room temperature.
Tie legs together with kitchen twine and pour 1 cup water into baking sheet.
Roast turkey, rotating pan halfway through, until skin is mostly golden brown all over, about 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, cook ¼ cup sherry vinegar or red wine vinegar, 2 Tbsp. honey, 4 tsp. Worcestershire sauce, 3 sprigs rosemary, 3 garlic cloves, crushed, two 2x1" strips orange zest, and remaining 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, room temperature, in a small saucepan over medium heat until bubbling and slightly thickened, about 5 minutes. Reduce heat to lowest setting and keep glaze warm.

Reduce oven temperature to 300° and continue to roast turkey, brushing with glaze every 30 minutes and adding more water by ½-cupfuls as needed to maintain some liquid in baking sheet, until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of breast near the neck registers 155° (don’t worry; the temperature will continue to climb while the bird rests), 65–85 minutes longer.

Skin should be deep golden brown, shiny, and crisp. Transfer turkey to a cutting board and let rest at least 30 minutes and up to 1 hour before carving. Editor’s note: The dry-brine turkey recipe was first printed in our November 2018 issue as ‘Dry-Rubbed Roast Turkey.
’ Head this way for more of our best Thanksgiving recipes →

items.name: Slow Cooker Turkey Breast with Gravy
ingredients: 1 ½ tablespoons unsalted butter ( or olive oil)
5 pound turkey breast (bone in, skin on (removed later), trimmed of fat)
steps: Melt butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion, carrot, celery and garlic and cook until onion is soft, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in flour and cook until golden, about 2 minutes. Stir in 1 cup of broth and scrape up any browned bits and smooth out any lumps; transfer to slow cooker.
Stir in remaining broth, water, wine, sage, and bay leaves into the slow cooker.
Season turkey with salt and pepper, place skin side up in the slow cooker, cover and cook 5 to 7 hours on low, or until the turkey reaches 165 degrees with an instant-read thermometer
Transfer turkey to a cutting board tent loosely with foil and let it rest 20 minutes.
Let braising liquid settle for 5 minutes, then remove the fat from the surface using a large spoon or a gravy fat separator.
Strain braising liquid into saucepan, discard celery, bay leaves and simmer until thickened, about 15 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Discard the skin and carve the turkey and serve with gravy.

items.name: Simple-Is-Best Stuffing
ingredients: ¾ cup (1½ sticks) unsalted butter plus more for baking dish
1 lb. good-quality day-old white bread, torn into 1" pieces (about 10 cups)
2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt
steps: Preheat oven to 250°. Grease a 13x9x2" baking dish with unsalted butter and set aside. Scatter 1 lb. good-quality day-old white bread, torn into 1" pieces (about 10 cups), in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet. Bake, stirring occasionally, until dried out, about 1 hour. Let cool; transfer to a very large bowl.

Meanwhile, melt ¾ cup unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat; add 2½ cups chopped yellow onions and 1½ cups ¼" slices celery to melted butter. Stir often until just beginning to brown, about 10 minutes. Add to bowl with dried bread; stir in ½ cup chopped flat-leaf parsley, 2 Tbsp.

chopped fresh sage, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh rosemary, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh thyme, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. freshly ground black pepper. Drizzle in 1¼ cups low-sodium chicken broth and toss gently. Let cool.

Preheat oven to 350°. Whisk 2 large eggs and remaining 1¼ cups low-sodium chicken broth in a small bowl. Add to bread mixture; fold gently until thoroughly combined. Transfer to prepared dish, cover with foil, and bake until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of dressing registers 160°, 35–40 minutes.

Uncover dressing; continue to bake until set and top is golden brown and crisp, 35–45 minutes longer. Do ahead: Dressing can be baked (before browning) 1 day ahead; uncover and let cool, then cover and chill. Uncover and bake until top is golden brown and crisp, 45–60 minutes. Leftover stuffing?

Use it up in our Winter Panzanella With Stuffing Croutons → Editor’s note: We first published this Thanksgiving stuffing recipe in our November 2012 issue as ‘Simple Is Best Dressing’; it has been updated for style. Head this way for more of our favorite Thanksgiving dinner side dishes→

items.name: BA’s Best Pumpkin Pie
ingredients: ¾ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
2 cups unsweetened pumpkin purée (from about 1¼ 15.oz. cans)
steps: Preheat oven to 425°. Roll out 1 disk Perfect Pie Crust on a lightly floured work surface to a 14" round. Transfer to a 9" pie dish. Pick up edges and allow dough to slump down into dish, letting excess dough hang over dish. Trim, leaving about a 1" overhang. Fold overhang under; pinch and crimp. Chill 30 minutes.

Line dough with parchment paper or foil, leaving some overhang. Fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake until crust is dry around the edges and just beginning to brown, 25–35 minutes. Carefully remove parchment and weights and reduce oven temperature to 350°.

Lightly beat 1 large egg, room temperature, in a small bowl just to blend, then brush over inside of crust (not the crimped edges) and continue to bake until crust is set and beginning to lightly brown in the center, 10–15 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack and let cool.
Do Ahead: Crust can be baked 1 day ahead; tightly wrap and store at room temperature.

Preheat oven to 325°. Lightly beat 1 large egg yolk, room temperature, and remaining 2 large eggs, room temperature, in a clean small bowl just to blend. Whisk ⅓ cup (67 g) sugar, 1 tsp. ground cinnamon, ¾ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, ½ tsp. ground ginger, ¼ tsp.

ground cloves, and ¼ tsp. ground nutmeg in a large bowl until no clumps remain. Add egg mixture, 2 cups unsweetened pumpkin purée, ⅔ cup sweetened condensed milk, ⅓ cup heavy cream, 2 Tbsp. maple syrup, and 2 tsp. vanilla extract and whisk until smooth. Pour into cooled crust.

Bake pie until edges are set and slightly puffed but center is recessed and wobbles like Jell-O, 60–75 minutes (it will continue to set after baking). Transfer to a wire rack and let cool at least 3 hours before slicing. Serve with whipped cream.

Do Ahead: Pie can be baked 1 day ahead; tightly wrap and chill. Serve warm or at room temperature. You can also freeze pumpkin pie up to 3 months in advance. Editor’s note: This recipe was first published in November 2016; it has been updated for style.
Head this way for more of our favorite Thanksgiving pies →

items.name: Buttered Nut Squash
ingredients: 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt
6 oz. thick-cut bacon, cut into 1" pieces
Zest and juice of 1 large lemon
steps: Place a rack in lower third of oven; preheat to 425°. Lightly crush 2 tsp. fennel seeds with a mortar and pestle or place on a cutting board and gently crush with a heavy pan. Peel 1 medium butternut squash (about 3 lb.) and halve lengthwise. Scoop out seeds; discard.

Cut squash into 2" irregular pieces, aiming for sharp, jagged shapes. Transfer to a large rimmed baking sheet; drizzle with 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil and sprinkle with fennel seeds, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. crushed red pepper flakes.
Toss squash to coat, arrange in a single layer, and roast until browned and tender, 30–35 minutes. Do Ahead: Squash can be roasted 2 hours ahead. Store at room temperature.

While the squash is roasting, cook 6 oz. thick-cut bacon, cut into 1" pieces, in a medium skillet over medium heat, stirring often, until browned and mostly crisp, 8–12 minutes. Transfer to a small plate with a slotted spoon.
Reduce heat to low; combine 1 cup raw pecans and 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter in same pan. Cook, stirring often, until butter browns and nuts have slightly darkened, 6–8 minutes. Remove from heat.

Stir in 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped (this will give it a head start to take off the raw edge), then add bacon, zest and juice of 1 large lemon, 3 sprigs sage, and 2 Tbsp. balsamic vinegar and stir to combine. Taste dressing and season with kosher salt if needed.
Arrange squash on a platter and spoon dressing over.

items.name: Gravy-Braised Turkey
ingredients: 4 whole turkey legs (thigh and drumstick; about 6½ lb. total), patted dry
2 heads of garlic, tops trimmed to expose cloves
1 small bunch thyme (about 10 sprigs), tied with kitchen twine
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 325°. Season 4 whole turkey legs (thigh and drumstick; about 6½ lb. total), patted dry, all over with kosher salt and freshly ground pepper. Heat 3 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large braiser or Dutch oven over medium-high.

Working in 2 batches if needed to avoid overcrowding, arrange turkey legs, skin side down, in pot and cook, undisturbed, rotating pan on burner a few times to ensure even browning, until browned underneath and they easily release from pot, 8–12 minutes.
Transfer turkey legs to a rimmed baking sheet, arranging skin side up. (No need to brown other side; turkey will still be raw at this point.)

Add more oil if pot looks dry; arrange 2 large oranges and/or lemons, halved, and 2 heads of garlic, tops trimmed to expose cloves, cut side down in pot and add 3 large shallots, peeled. Cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 2–3 minutes. Transfer each to baking sheet with turkey as they are done (it’s okay if some fall apart slightly).

Add 6 Tbsp. (¾ stick) unsalted butter to pot and cook until melted. Sprinkle in ⅓ cup (42 g) all-purpose flour and cook, stirring constantly, until no pockets of dry flour remain, about 1 minute. Gradually pour in 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth, stirring constantly to combine.
Bring to a simmer and cook until gravy is just starting to thicken, about 2 minutes. Stir in 3 Tbsp. Worcestershire sauce and season with salt and pepper.

Nestle turkey legs into gravy, skin side up, then tuck oranges, garlic, and shallots around, arranging oranges and garlic cut side up. Add 1 small bunch thyme (about 10 sprigs), tied with kitchen twine, and cover pot tightly with a lid or foil. Braise 2 hours.

(If your pot is too small to comfortably fit everything, transfer gravy to a 13x9" baking dish before adding turkey legs and aromatics.) Uncover pot and continue to bake until turkey legs are deeply browned, meat shreds easily off the bone, and gravy has thickened a little, 45–55 minutes.

Let turkey and gravy cool slightly before serving. Transfer to a platter if desired. (If gravy has excess fat on top, skim off with a spoon and discard before serving or spooning over legs on platter.)

items.name: Thanksgiving Cornbread
ingredients: ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, plus more for pan
1 green bell pepper, halved, ribs and seeds removed, finely chopped
1 lb. spicy and/or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt
¼ cup finely chopped sage, thyme, and/or rosemary
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 400°. Line a 13x9" baking pan with parchment paper, leaving generous overhang on long sides. Coat pan and parchment with unsalted butter. Melt ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat, then pour into a small bowl.

Cook 1 green bell pepper, halved, ribs and seeds removed, finely chopped, 1 medium white onion, finely chopped, and 2 celery stalks, finely chopped, in same skillet, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 1 lb.

spicy and/or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, and cook, breaking up and stirring occasionally, until browned (it may still be a little raw in the center at this point), about 5 minutes. Remove from heat.

Stir together 4 cups (624 g) fine-ground yellow cornmeal, 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour, 1 cup (200 g) sugar, 1 Tbsp. plus 1½ tsp. baking powder, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 tsp. baking soda, and ¼ cup finely chopped sage, thyme, and/or rosemary in a large bowl.

Gradually pour in 3½ cups buttermilk, then melted butter, stirring constantly until combined. Add 4 large eggs one at a time, mixing to incorporate after each addition. Fold in sausage mixture, then scrape batter into prepared pan.

Bake cornbread, rotating pan front to back halfway through, until golden brown and top springs back when gently pressed, 38–45 minutes. Let cool in pan 15 minutes. Using parchment paper overhang, lift cornbread out of pan and transfer to a cutting board. Cut into 12–18 slices; arrange on a platter. Do Ahead: Cornbread can be baked 4 hours ahead. Store at room temperature; cut just before serving.

items.name: A Beautiful Cabbage Galette
ingredients: 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for surface
2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces
10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick
1 medium head of savoy cabbage (1¾–2¼ lb.)
1 medium white or yellow onion, thinly sliced
½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
5 oz. Gruyère or sharp cheddar, coarsely grated
steps: Whisk 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, ¼ tsp. baking powder, and 1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour in a large bowl. Add 2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces, and rub in with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy). Add 10 Tbsp.

chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea size). Make a well in the center and pour in ¼ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute.
Knead dough in bowl just to bring together (some dry bits may remain).

Turn dough out onto a lightly dusted surface and sprinkle with all-purpose flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again. Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting dough with more flour as needed to prevent sticking.

Pat into a ½"-thick disk and wrap tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours. Do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

When dough is almost done chilling, cut 1 medium head of savoy cabbage (1¾–2¼ lb.) in half and cut out triangular core at bottom; discard. Separate leaves and tear into pieces about the size of your palm. Transfer about half to a large bowl and set aside.

Melt 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 medium white or yellow onion, thinly sliced, and season generously with kosher salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and starting to turn translucent, about 5 minutes. Add remaining 1 Tbsp.

unsalted butter and ¾ tsp. cumin seeds (if using) and cook until butter is melted. Add remaining cabbage leaves and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is translucent and lightly browned and cabbage is wilted, 18–22 minutes.
Transfer to a large plate or a small baking sheet; chill in fridge or freezer until cool.

Place a rack in bottom third of oven; preheat to 400°. Whisk 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, ⅓ cup heavy cream, 2 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a measuring glass to combine. Pour cream mixture over reserved raw cabbage leaves and toss with your hands to coat. Add 5 oz. Gruyère or sharp cheddar, coarsely grated, and toss again to combine.
Unwrap dough and roll out on a lightly floured sheet of parchment paper to a 13–14" round (some dough will extend beyond the parchment). Transfer on parchment paper to a baking sheet.

Spread cooked cabbage mixture over dough, leaving about a 1½" border around edges. Fold dough up and over filling, folding and tucking as needed to make a rustic border. Pile raw cabbage mixture on top of cooked cabbage mixture to make a dramatic heap. (It will look ridiculously high at first but will cook down when it bakes.)

Bake galette 25 minutes. Rotate baking sheet front to back, reduce heat to 375°, and bake until cabbage and crust are deep golden brown, 25–35 minutes. (If cabbage seems to be browning too much, reduce heat to 350° toward the end.

) Let galette cool on baking sheet at least 1 hour and up to 4 hours before serving. Do Ahead: Sautéed cabbage can be made 1 day ahead. Transfer to an airtight container and chill. Tightly wrap undressed raw cabbage in plastic and chill.

items.name: Pear Salad With Honey-Roasted Seeds
ingredients: ¾ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
1 cup raw sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds (pepitas), and/or coarsely crushed raw nuts (such as walnuts, almonds, and/or hazelnuts)
2 lb. firm green pears (such as Bartlett and/or Anjou; about 4 large), cored, thinly sliced
2 oz. Parmesan, aged white cheddar, or Manchego cheese, shaved
steps: Preheat oven to 325°. Whisk 3 Tbsp. honey, 1 tsp. garlic powder, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, and ¾ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl to combine.

Add 1 cup raw sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds (pepitas), and/or coarsely crushed raw nuts (such as walnuts, almonds, and/or hazelnuts) and stir to coat. Spread out in a single layer on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet; reserve bowl.
Bake seed mixture until golden brown, 12–14 minutes. (Honey mixture will puff up a bit but will deflate when you stir.) Toss honey-roasted seeds, then let cool. Toss again just to break up.

Whisk 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp. Dijon mustard, a pinch of kosher salt, and remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in reserved bowl. Add 2 lb. firm green pears (such as Bartlett and/or Anjou; about 4 large), cored, thinly sliced, to dressing and gently toss to coat.

Arrange pears on a large flat platter. Scatter honey-roasted seeds over and top with 2 oz. Parmesan, aged white cheddar, or Manchego cheese, shaved. Do Ahead: Honey-roasted seeds can be made 6 hours ahead. Store at room temperature.

items.name: Collard Greens Vinaigrette
ingredients: 2 bunches collard greens, ribs and stems removed, leaves cut into 2" pieces
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, plus more
⅓ cup plus 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil
¼ cup (packed) coarsely chopped tarragon, plus leaves for serving
2 tsp. sugar, plus more for walnuts
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 325°. Toast ½ cup raw walnuts on a rimmed baking sheet, tossing halfway through, until golden brown, 10–12 minutes.

Meanwhile, cook 2 bunches collard greens, ribs and stems removed, leaves cut into 2" pieces, in a large pot of generously salted boiling water until just tender, 9–11 minutes. Using tongs, immediately transfer to a large bowl of ice water and let cool.

Whisk 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, ¼ cup white wine vinegar, 2 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, preferably country-style, ⅓ cup extra-virgin olive oil, ¼ cup (packed) coarsely chopped tarragon, 2 tsp. sugar, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl to combine. Set dressing aside.

Transfer toasted walnuts to a small bowl and drizzle with remaining 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Sprinkle with a generous pinch each of sugar and salt and toss to coat. Taste and add more sugar if needed (nuts should be more sweet than salty). Set seasoned walnuts aside.
Drain collard greens and squeeze gently to remove excess water. Transfer to bowl with reserved dressing and toss to coat evenly. Cover and chill at least 15 minutes and up to 2 hours.

Arrange greens in a shallow bowl or on a platter and spoon any dressing remaining in bowl over. Top with seasoned walnuts and tarragon leaves. Do Ahead: Walnuts can be toasted and dressing can be made 1 day ahead. Store walnuts airtight at room temperature. Cover dressing and chill.

items.name: Chicken Corn Chowder
ingredients: 1 lb. Yukon gold potatoes diced, (about 2 potatoes, 3½ cups) $0.96***
¼ tsp black pepper freshly cracked,
steps: Gather and prep all ingredients.
In a large pot or Dutch oven, cook bacon over medium heat until crisp. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and leave the rendered fat in the pot.
Add onion, garlic, carrots, celery, and red bell pepper to the bacon fat. Cook for 5-6 minutes until softened.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and cook, stirring constantly for 1-2 minutes to remove the raw flour taste.

Slowly whisk in the chicken broth. Stir in diced potatoes, chicken breasts, smoked paprika, thyme, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, until potatoes are tender and chicken is cooked through.
Remove chicken from the pot, shred with two forks, and set aside.
Carefully remove about half of the vegetables and broth, add ½ cup of corn, and puree until smooth. Return the puree to the pot.
Add shredded chicken, the remaining corn, apple cider vinegar, and chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed.
Garnish with crumbled bacon and optional green onions. Serve warm with crusty bread.

items.name: Black Bean Soup
ingredients: 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, plus more to serve
4 (15-ounce) cans black beans, rinsed and drained (about 6 cups)
1 to 2 limes, plus more to serve
1 to 2 green onions trimmed and sliced (both white and green parts)
steps: Sauté the vegetables. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the onion, carrots, celery, and both bell peppers. Season with a big pinch of kosher salt and black pepper. Cook, stirring regularly, until softened, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Bloom the aromatics. Add the garlic, cumin, oregano, and cayenne and cook, stirring,until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Simmer. Add the black beans, 4 cups broth, and the bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partially covered, for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Blend. Remove the bay leaf. Use an immersion blender to purée part of the soup, leaving plenty of whole beans. (Or blend 2 cups in a blender and stir it back in.) If it's too thick, add up to 1 more cup of broth.

Finish and serve. Stir in juice of 1 lime and the cilantro. Taste and adjust salt and pepper or add more lime juice if needed. Ladle into bowls, drizzle with olive oil, and serve with the toppings of your choice.

items.name: Beef Enchilada Casserole
ingredients: 1 medium green bell pepper cored and chopped
1 medium red bell pepper cored and chopped
1 pound lean ground beef I used 90%
1 (15-ounce can) reduced sodium black beans, rinsed and drained
8 ounces Colby Jack or Montery jack cheese grated (2 cups)
Optional for serving: sliced jalapeño, sliced avocado, lime juice, diced tomato, plain Greek yogurt or sour cream, chopped fresh cilantro
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Coat a 9×13-inch casserole dish with baking spray.
Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Add the onion, green bell pepper, and red bell pepper. Sauté until the vegetables are starting to become tender, about 10 minutes.
Add the beef, cumin, garlic powder, oregano, and salt. Cook, breaking the beef into small crumbles, until no pink remains, about 6 minutes.
Stir in 1 cup of the enchilada sauce, black beans, and green chiles. Simmer and stir until thickened, about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat.
Pour the remaining sauce into a wide shallow bowl (a pie plate works well). Spread ¼ cup of it into a thin layer across the bottom of the prepared dish.

Working one at a time using tongs, dip 4 tortillas in the sauce, turning to coat both sides and letting the excess drip off. Arrange them in the dish, staggering them so most of the bottom of the dish is covered.
Spread one-third of the beef mixture over the tortillas, then sprinkle with ½ cup cheese.
Repeat: 4 dipped tortillas (try to offset the staggering with the layer below so the tortillas cover open gaps the first did not), half of the remaining beef, ½ cup cheese.

For the final layer, dip and arrange the final 4 tortillas and spread with the remaining beef. Pour any remaining sauce over the top and sprinkle with the remaining 1 cup cheese. Cover the pan tightly with foil.
Bake 25 minutes. Remove the foil and bake 10 minutes more, until hot and bubbly and the cheese is melted.
Let rest at least 10 minutes to set up before slicing. Serve hot with toppings of choice.

items.name: One-Pan Chicken and Gravy with Potatoes and Vegetables
ingredients: 1 – 1.25kg (2 – 2.5lb) large bone-in skin-on thighs (4 – 5 pieces) , ~220-250g / 7 – 8 oz each (Note 1)
½ tsp onion powder , or more garlic powder
1 tsp dried thyme , crushed with fingers
1 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt (halve for table salt, double for flakes)
600g/ 20oz baby potatoes , skin on, cut into 1.75 cm / 0.7" pieces (Note 2)
3 carrots , peeled, cut into 7mm / ⅓" thick coins (consider halving very big rounds into half moons)
1 large red onion , cut into 1cm / 0.4″ thick wedges
2 garlic cloves , crushed with garlic crusher or finely minced with a knife
⅓ cup plain flour / all-purpose flour
2 ½ cups beef stock/broth , low sodium (yes, beef, not chicken! Note 3)
1 tsp dark soy *secret ingredient* , optional, to make gravy rich brown plus deepens flavour, or use gravy browner (Note 4)
1 cup frozen peas , leave out to thaw while chicken is baking
1 tsp thyme leaves , for sprinkling (100% optional)
steps: Toss Potato & Veg ingredients in bowl, pour into pan. Coat chicken with olive oil then sprinkle with Seasoning. Place on Veg. Whisk flour with bit of stock, then whisk in everything else and rest of stock. Pour in pan, drizzle chicken with oil, bake 45 min at 200°C/390°F (180°C fan). Remove chicken, stir in peas, serve!
Preheat the oven to 200°C/390°F (180°C fan-forced).
Potato & veg – Toss the Potato and Vegetable ingredients in a bowl. Pour into a roasting pan (mine is 35 x 26cm/13.8 x 10.2").
Season chicken – Put the chicken in the same bowl , drizzle with the oil and turn to coat. Mix the Seasoning in a bowl then sprinkle evenly on the chicken, using most on the skin side.
Place on top of the vegetables, bundling the chicken into neat parcels by tucking the flapping bits under.

Gravy – Put the flour in the same bowl then add about ½ cup of the stock. Whisk until lump free, then whisk in the rest of the stock and remaining Gravy ingredients. Pour into the pan down the edge (don't pour over chicken or veg).
Bake 45 minutes – Drizzle the chicken with a little bit of olive oil then bake for 45 minutes.

Stir in peas – Remove the chicken onto a plate. Add the thawed peas then use a rubber spatula to stir the gravy and vegetables – this will make the liquid come together into a lovely thick gravy. (See Note 5 if gravy is too thick or thin).
Serve! – Divide vegetables and gravy between bowls, top with chicken and enjoy!

items.name: Creamed Corn
ingredients: 8 cups sweet yellow corn kernels (fresh or frozen, about 2 ½ pounds, thawed if frozen)
2 teaspoons kosher salt (divided, plus additional to taste)
½ small yellow onion (about 4 ounces, finely chopped (about ¾ cup))
steps: In a blender, combine 2 cups of corn, the milk, cream cheese, and 1 ½ teaspoons salt. Blend until smooth then set the corn milk aside.

In a large saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the onion, season with the remaining ½ teaspoon of salt, and cook, stirring frequently, until tender, 4 to 5 minutes. If the butter starts to brown before the onion is tender, reduce the heat slightly.

Add the garlic and cook, stirring constantly, until tender, about 1 minute. Add the remaining 6 cups of corn and cook until the corn is hot, stirring occasionally, 3 to 4 minutes, if frozen, or 5 minutes if fresh.

Add the corn milk and a couple grinds of black pepper, stir to combine, and slowly warm the mixture until it starts to bubble, 6 to 8 minutes, stirring frequently. Resist turning up the heat since this might cause the corn milk to scorch.

Continue to cook, stirring and scraping the sides of the saucepan frequently and adjusting the heat as needed to maintain gently bubbling, until the corn milk has reduced slightly and the mixture is thickened and creamy, 10 to 15 minutes.
Transfer the creamed corn to a large serving bowl, sprinkle with the chives, and serve.

items.name: Bourbon Caramel Apple Pie
ingredients: 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt
4 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces
1¼ cups (2½ sticks) chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick
Rice flour or all-purpose flour (for surface)
3 lb. Honeycrisp apples (about 6 large), peeled, cored, quartered, thinly sliced crosswise
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
steps: Whisk 3⅓ cups (417 g) all-purpose flour, 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ½ tsp. baking powder in a large bowl to combine. Add 4 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces; rub into dry ingredients with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy).
Add 1¼ cups (2½ sticks) chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash with your fingers into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea-size).

Make a well in the center of mixture and pour in ½ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute, then knead in bowl a couple of times to bring dough together (some dry bits may remain).

Turn out dough onto a surface lightly dusted with rice flour or all-purpose flour; dust top of dough with flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold dough in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again.

Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting with more flour as needed to prevent sticking. Divide dough in half and pat each piece into a ½"-thick disk. Wrap each disk tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.
Do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap each disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

Place 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar and ½ cup water in a medium Dutch oven or other heavy pot and cover. Bring to a boil over medium heat (no need to stir); cook until sugar is dissolved, 4–7 minutes total. Uncover and continue to cook, stirring or swirling pot occasionally, until caramel turns a deep golden brown, 10–12 minutes.

Add zest of 1 lemon, 3 lb. Honeycrisp apples (about 6 large), peeled, cored, quartered, thinly sliced crosswise, ½ cup bourbon, 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. ground cinnamon to caramel (it may become stiff).

Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until caramel dissolves and apples have released a generous amount of liquid and are tender but still retain their shape (they should look mostly translucent), 15–18 minutes.

Stir ⅓ cup heavy cream, 3 Tbsp. cornstarch, and 2 Tbsp. cool water in a small bowl until cornstarch is dissolved. Pour into apple mixture and cook (it should be bubbling), stirring often, until mixture is thick, about 5 minutes. Transfer filling to a large bowl; let cool. Cover and chill until cold, at least 45 minutes.

Meanwhile, let dough sit at room temperature 5 minutes. Unwrap 1 disk and roll out on a surface lightly dusted with rice flour or all-purpose flour to a 12" round, about ¼" thick. Brush excess flour from dough and wrap around rolling pin.
Transfer to a 9"-diameter pie pan (such as East Fork Spun Iron Pie Dish). Unfurl into pan, then lift edges and allow dough to slump down into pan. Trim, leaving about a 1" overhang. Chill 15 minutes.

Unwrap remaining disk; roll out on surface lightly dusted with more rice flour to a 18x12" rectangle, about ⅛" thick. Brush excess flour from dough and transfer to a large parchment-lined baking sheet.

Brush dough with a thin film of cold water; sprinkle remaining ¼ cup (50 g) granulated sugar over and press gently with your hands to cover dough completely in an even layer (coating dough before cutting into strips will give you the most even coverage). Chill 15 minutes.

Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 375°. Spoon chilled filling into pie pan and smooth surface to level. Using a ruler, cut dough rectangle into 1"-wide strips. Lay 5–8 strips over filling, spacing evenly across surface to cover.

Weave another 5–8 strips over, then under, alternating to create a lattice crust (you may not use all of the strips). Trim overhang to match bottom crust. Press edges of top and bottom crusts firmly together to seal, then trim again, leaving about ¼" overhang.
Fold overhang up and over lattice so crust is flush with edges of pan and crimp as desired with lightly floured fingers.

Place pan on a rimmed baking sheet (to catch drips) and bake pie until crust is set and golden, 45–50 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 350°; continue to bake until crust is deep golden brown and filling is bubbling up through lattice, 40–50 minutes more.

Transfer pan to a wire rack and let pie cool in pan at least 4 hours before serving. Do Ahead: Filling can be made 2 days ahead; keep chilled. Pie can be baked 1 day ahead; store, loosely covered, at room temperature.

items.name: Salted Coffee Custard Pie
ingredients: 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, plus more, room temperature, for pan
¼ cup (packed; 50 g) dark brown sugar
1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
2 Tbsp. instant espresso powder, plus more for serving (optional)
2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1 tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided
½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled
1 Tbsp. plus 1 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract
steps: Place a rack in middle of oven and preheat to 350°. Butter pie dish with unsalted butter. Pulse 2 cups (180 g) old-fashioned oats, ¼ cup (31 g) all-purpose flour, ¼ cup (packed; 50 g) dark brown sugar, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp.

Morton kosher salt in a food processor until oats are coarsely ground. Drizzle in 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled; pulse just until mixture comes together. Transfer to prepared dish (such as East Fork Ceramic Pie Plate); wipe out and reserve food processor.

Press crust firmly and evenly across bottom and up sides of dish with a flat-bottomed measuring cup. Bake until golden and surface looks dry, 25–30 minutes. Transfer crust to a wire rack; reduce oven temperature to 325°.

Pulse 1 cup (packed; 200 g) dark brown sugar, 2 Tbsp. all-purpose flour, 2 Tbsp. instant espresso powder, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in food processor until no lumps remain, about 1 minute.

Add 3 large eggs, ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, and 1 Tbsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract and pulse until smooth. Add 1 cup cold-brew coffee concentrate and 2 cups heavy cream and pulse until well combined.

Pour custard into crust (it’s okay if crust is still warm). Bake pie until edges of filling are set and slightly puffed but center still wobbles a little when gently shaken, 40–50 minutes (filling will continue to set after baking). Transfer to a wire rack; let cool at least 3 hours, or, preferably, chill 12 hours.

Using an electric mixer, beat ½ cup mascarpone, 4 Tbsp. granulated sugar, remaining 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, ⅔ cup heavy cream, and 1 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract in a medium bowl until soft peaks form. Spoon whipped cream mixture over pie; swirl lightly to create divots and peaks.

Just before serving, dust with instant espresso powder if desired; sprinkle generously with flaky sea salt. Do ahead: Pie (without espresso powder and sea salt garnishes) can be made 1 day ahead. Cover loosely and keep chilled.

items.name: Cranberry Meringue Pie
ingredients: 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt
2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces
10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick
Rice flour or all-purpose flour (for surface)
1½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, divided
¾ cup (1½ sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces
steps: Whisk 1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour, 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ¼ tsp. baking powder in a large bowl to combine. Add 2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces, and rub into dry ingredients with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy).
Add 10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash with your fingers into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea-size).

Make a well in the center of mixture and pour in ¼ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute, then knead in bowl a couple of times to bring dough together (some dry bits may remain).

Turn out dough onto a surface lightly dusted with rice flour or all-purpose flour and dust top of dough with flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold dough in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again.

Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting with more rice flour as needed to prevent sticking. Pat into a ½"-thick disk and wrap tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.

Let dough disk sit at room temperature 5 minutes. Roll out dough on a lightly floured surface to a 12" round, about ¼" thick. Brush excess flour from dough and wrap around rolling pin. Transfer to a 9"-diameter pie pan (such as East Fork Spun Iron Pie Dish).

Unfurl into pan, then lift edges and allow dough to slump down into pan. Trim, leaving about a 1½" overhang. Fold overhang under so crust is flush with edges of pan and crimp as desired with lightly floured fingers.
Set pan on a rimmed baking sheet and prick bottom and sides of crust with a fork in several places. Freeze, uncovered, at least 30 minutes and up to 2 hours.

Place a rack in lower third of oven; preheat to 400°. Line crust with a sheet of parchment paper and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake crust, tenting edges with foil if browning too quickly, until edges are set and look dry, 20–25 minutes.

Carefully lift out parchment paper and weights and continue baking crust, gently pressing bottom and sides occasionally with a flat-bottomed measuring cup if puffing up, until bottom looks dry and is golden, 20–25 minutes more. Transfer pan to a wire rack and let crust cool.
Do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

Bring 1 lb. fresh or frozen cranberries, 1½ cups (300 g) granulated sugar, and ¼ cup water to a boil in a large saucepan, then reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring often, until cranberries soften and burst and most of the liquid has evaporated, 10–15 minutes. Let cranberry mixture cool.

Transfer cranberry mixture to a blender; reserve pan. Add ⅔ cup fresh lime juice and ¼ cup (32 g) cornstarch and blend on high speed until smooth. Scrape purée back into pan (not over heat) and add 3 large eggs, 2 large egg yolks, 1 Tbsp. vanilla extract, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp.

Morton kosher salt. Place over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until mixture bubbles and thickens to a pudding-like consistency, about 4 minutes. Remove pan from heat. Add ¾ cup (1½ sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces, and whisk until melted and combined.

Strain curd through a fine-mesh sieve, pushing with a rubber spatula, directly into crust. Smooth into an even layer and cover with plastic wrap, pressing directly onto surface. Chill pie at least 4 hours and up to 1 day.
Just before serving, beat 6 large egg whites, room temperature, ¼ tsp. cream of tartar, remaining 1¼ cups (250 g) granulated sugar, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp.

Morton kosher salt in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment on medium speed until foamy and sugar is dissolved, about 5 minutes. Increase speed to high and continue to beat until stiff peaks form, about 3 minutes more.
Spoon meringue over filling and swirl decoratively as desired. Using a kitchen torch, toast meringue if desired.
